record.title: RECAP uses dependency-aware step credit to reduce reasoning tokens in math models
record.summary: The arXiv preprint introduces RECAP, which gives GRPO training step-level credit using LLM-annotated semantic dependencies plus a gold-answer likelihood signal. On Qwen2.5-Math-7B, the authors report 2.0–3.7 percentage-point pass@1 gains and 8–31% fewer reasoning tokens than GRPO across GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME 2024 and AIME 2025. Results on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B are mixed, so the paper does not establish a uniform cross-model improvement. These are author-reported experiments, not independently reproduced; the tested regime is limited to two 7B math models and four benchmarks.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors introduce RECAP, a GRPO-based reasoning-training method that combines backward-propagated responsibility on LLM-annotated semantic dependency graphs with step efficacy measured by changes in gold-answer log-likelihood. The method does not require a separately trained process reward model or preconstructed concise traces.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On Qwen2.5-Math-7B across GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME 2024 and AIME 2025, the authors report RECAP improves pass@1 by 2.0–3.7 percentage points and reduces reasoning tokens by 8–31% relative to GRPO; the paper reports eight-run variability for its main table.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper also evaluates DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B. RECAP uses fewer tokens than GRPO across the four reported benchmarks, but accuracy is mixed and stronger baselines outperform it on several cells; this does not establish a uniform gain across models.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors’ trace analysis attributes token savings primarily to fewer reasoning operations and less dead-end reasoning rather than shorter expression; their dependency-edge labels and analysis use model-assisted annotation.

contradictory_evidence: On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, RECAP is not uniformly more accurate than GRPO or the strongest compared methods; the paper’s claimed gains are model- and benchmark-dependent.

evidence_gaps.description: No publicly linked executable implementation or data artifact was verified during this review, and the research desk did not reproduce the training or evaluation results.
Evaluation is confined to two 7B math-oriented models and four mathematics benchmarks; effectiveness on general reasoning, coding, multilingual or frontier-scale models is unknown.
Semantic dependency labels rely on LLM-assisted annotation; annotation error and sensitivity to annotator model may affect the credit signal.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported efficiency gains generalize beyond the tested math models and datasets, dependency-aware step credit could improve reasoning post-training choices by lowering inference tokens while preserving or improving accuracy. Four benchmark results on two 7B models make this notable, but the evidence is author-reported and the regime remains narrow.
limitations: The source is an author-reported arXiv preprint; no independent reproduction was performed.
The clearest accuracy-and-token result is on Qwen2.5-Math-7B and four math benchmarks; DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B results are mixed.
The method depends on LLM-annotated semantic dependencies and answer likelihood, adding annotation and model-scoring cost not summarized here as end-to-end deployment economics.
The reported reduction is in reasoning tokens; it does not by itself establish lower wall-clock latency, energy use or cost per solved task.
No code artifact or independent baseline audit was verified in this activation.
brief.summary: The arXiv preprint introduces RECAP, which gives GRPO training step-level credit using LLM-annotated semantic dependencies plus a gold-answer likelihood signal. On Qwen2.5-Math-7B, the authors report 2.0–3.7 percentage-point pass@1 gains and 8–31% fewer reasoning tokens than GRPO across GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME 2024 and AIME 2025. Results on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B are mixed, so the paper does not establish a uniform cross-model improvement. These are author-reported experiments, not independently reproduced; the tested regime is limited to two 7B math models and four benchmarks.

technical.claimed_result: For Qwen2.5-Math-7B, the authors report RECAP pass@1 at 87.7% on GSM8K, 74.2% on MATH-500, 26.7% on AIME 2024 and 12.5% on AIME 2025, with lower completion tokens than GRPO on all four. The paper summarizes gains of 2.0–3.7 percentage points and token reductions of 8–31% relative to GRPO. For DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, token use is lower than GRPO, but accuracy gains are not uniform and DDCA/LEASH lead on several benchmarks.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper reports reasoning-token counts, not wall-clock inference, energy or cost per solved task. Training and annotation/scoring overhead were not independently measured in this review.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected preprint describes the method, four benchmark comparisons for each of two 7B models, and author-reported run variability. the research desk did not reproduce the training or evaluation.
technical.mechanism: RECAP segments each generated trace into steps, uses an LLM to annotate support, context and restatement dependencies in a directed acyclic graph, propagates responsibility backward from the final answer, and combines that structural credit with changes in gold-answer log-likelihood to reshape GRPO advantages.
technical.regime: Author-run mathematical reasoning experiments using Qwen2.5-Math-7B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B across GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME 2024 and AIME 2025. These results do not establish performance on general reasoning, coding, multilingual tasks or larger frontier models.
technical.reproducibility: The paper gives algorithm, training/evaluation details and prompts in its appendices and reports eight-run variability for the main table. No code/data artifact was verified here, and no independent reproduction was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: GRPO is the direct baseline used for the reported 2.0–3.7 point accuracy and 8–31% token comparison on Qwen2.5-Math-7B. Other methods sometimes score higher, and results on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B are mixed.

brief.title: RECAP uses dependency-aware step credit to reduce reasoning tokens in math models
brief.why_it_matters: Reasoning tokens can dominate inference budgets for long mathematical traces. If RECAP’s reported trade-off reproduces and transfers, it could change post-training choices by rewarding steps according to both their downstream use and their progress toward a correct answer. The current paper supports a bounded research result, not a general claim that dependency-aware credit improves reasoning across models or tasks.
